title: Grateful Dead Live at International Amphitheatre on 1973-02-19
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Samplitude Professional v8.01 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Ampex C-90) -> Dat (44.1k) D

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording captures a monster Feb‑19‑1973 second set with a seamless jam from He's Gone through China Doll, highlighted by Phil’s thunderous bass and Jerry’s pristine tone.
ai_review.review: The SBD capture is clean, crisp and well‑balanced, letting the band’s legendary February ’73 improvisations shine. Reviewers rave about the 70‑minute run – He’s Gone → Truckin’ → The Other One → Eyes of the World → China Doll – plus a rousing Sugar Magnolia and Casey Jones, noting Phil Lesh’s “lead‑bass” throughout and Jerry Garcia’s flawless guitar and vocal delivery. A lone negative comment mentions poor venue acoustics for the missing first set, but overall the performance is celebrated as one of ’73’s finest.

ai_rating.rationale: Over a dozen enthusiastic reviews praise both musical performance and recording clarity; only one low‑rating comment concerns venue acoustics, not the audio source.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clean, crisp mix with balanced instrument levels; no dropout or muddiness reported. Listeners note the sound is ‘clean even at volume’ and praise Miller’s capture.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A continuous, high‑energy jam sequence lasting ~70 minutes that moves fluidly from He's Gone into Truckin', then The Other One, Eyes of the World and China Doll before closing with a fiery Sugar Magnolia and Casey Jones.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for perfect tone, emotive guitar work and clear vocals, especially on China Doll.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as ‘kicks ass’, ‘lead‑bass from start to finish’, and the highlight of the show; his playing is called a peak era moment.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s cymbals noted for shimmering crash; overall drum work considered solid but not specifically highlighted.
